newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government pledges help for flood victims.
newsitem.headline: Polish government pledges help for flood victims.

text.p: The Polish government decided on Thursday to squeeze out 500 million zlotys from various budget reserves to help victims of the country's heavy flooding, which had claimed at least 22 lives.

"We are able to earmark about 500 million zlotys for the removal of the damage done by flooding without changes in current regulations and the budget law," Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz told the main television news.
Cimoszewicz, speaking after a meeting with officials responsible for the rescue operations, said the government would soon prepare a strategic plan to repair the damage done by the flooding.

Opposition parties, hoping to unseat the ruling ex-communists in the September parliamentary elections, had heavily criticised Cimoszewicz and his cabinet for failing to offer any substantial financial aid.

The flood wave, a result of five days of heavy rain in the south of the country, put a total of 3,100 square km (1,200 sq miles) under water. Some 20,000 people were forced out of their homes and the number of evacuees was growing.
No official estimates of the size of the damage were yet available.
Authorities sent more than 15,000 firefighters, soldiers, border guards and policemen to the rescue efforts, along with 20 helicopters and 160 boats.
But the oppostion and many media have accused the central and local authorities of mishandling the rescue operation.

The flooding robbed the ruling left of moments of glory as celebrations of Poland's invitation to join NATO highlighted by U.S. President Bill Clinton's visit to Warsaw were knocked off the front pages by reports on the disaster.
